status: DRAFT — pre-validation. No rule in this file is production-approved. Rules with provisional=true or threshold=null MUST NOT be treated as validated engineering limits.
units: mm, kg, N, N/mm2 unless stated

materials.standard: Core: EN 312 type P2 (furniture, dry conditions). Surface: EN 14322.

moe_bending_Nmm2.note: Standard minimum — conservative E for deflection calcs until supplier datasheet value confirmed

materials.moisture: Service class 1, dry interior only. Particleboard swells irreversibly when wetted (Rae 2001 p.34, tier 4).
materials.screw_holding: Poor for conventional wood screws; use confirmat/deep-thread or cam+dowel (Rae 2001 pp.33, 83, tier 4).

materials.standard: EN 622-5 (fibreboard) — confirm exact grade with supplier
materials.note: Alternative 5 mm for larger backs; thresholds unresolved.

hardware.reassembly: good — designed for repeated knock-down cycles

withdrawal_force_N.note: ~1400 N reported in trade sources for laminated PB, 25 mm engagement — NOT validated; do not use in engineering calcs

hardware.reassembly: limited — repeated driving into same particleboard hole degrades grip; prefer cams for customer re-assembly (Rae p.83 tier 4 for suitability; degradation = tier 5 practice)
hardware.source: Häfele 7×50 confirmat product data; trade drilling guides

hardware.role: Alignment + shear; carries shear so cams only clamp (tier 5 practice)

rated_load_per_pin_kg.source: Häfele K-Line shelf support P-00861954 (15.6 kg/item)
rated_load_per_pin_kg.note: Generic steel pins commonly rated ~11 kg (25 lb) — use the rating of the actually purchased SKU

count_rule.source: Blum EASY ASSEMBLY blog 'Number of hinges' (blum.com)

hardware.status: requires_validation (cup depth + exact chart from Blum catalogue for chosen hinge)

hardware.name: Drawer runner, dynamic load class 25–30 kg (Blum TANDEM / Hettich class)
hardware.source: Blum TANDEM programme (30/50 kg dynamic load classes)
hardware.status: requires_validation (choose SKU; min cabinet depth = nominal length + clearance)

hardware.name: Anti-tip wall attachment device + instructions
hardware.source: EN 14749:2016+A1:2022 — wall attachment provisions & strength test of attachment device
hardware.status: requires_validation (select device; lab test per EN 14749; wall-side fixings explicitly excluded from standard)

shelf_uniform_design_load_kg_dm2.source: EN 16122:2012 shelf loading (0.65 kg/dm² of shelf area) — used as default design load ('books')

deflection_limit.value: 1.7 mm per 300 mm of span (≈0.02 in/ft), and never > span/200
deflection_limit.note: Cosmetic/quality limit, not a safety limit. Validate against EN 16122 deflection reporting and physical tests.

rules.name: Supported MVP product categories
rules.description: Only these categories are configurable in MVP: open shelving units, bookcases, small/medium cabinets with doors, bedside tables, storage units, simple desks/tables of panel construction.
rules.rationale: Panel-carcass furniture is the lowest-risk, best-understood scope for 18 mm LTD frameless construction. Casework principles are well documented (Hylton pp.84–93; Rae pp.45–57).

user_message.en: This furniture type isn’t available yet. We currently support shelves, bookcases, cabinets, bedside tables, storage units and simple desks.

rules.test_method: product decision
rules.notes: Excluded from MVP: seating (EN 12520/16139 test burden), beds & bunk beds (EN 1725 / EN 747), children's furniture & cots (EN 716; child-safety exposure), wall-hung cabinets (anchorage into unknown walls; EN 14749 wall-unit tests), wardrobes >2200 mm, glass elements.

rules.name: Hard-block safety-critical categories
rules.description: Chairs, stools, beds, bunk/loft beds, cots and any product marketed for children under 3 cannot be created or approximated (e.g. a 'shelf' proportioned as a ladder/steps).
rules.rationale: These carry dedicated EN safety standards with mandatory physical testing regimes that Myble has not performed.

sources.ref: EN 12520, EN 1725, EN 747-1/2, EN 716-1/2 (existence of dedicated regimes)

rules.condition: category in blocked_list OR heuristic step/ladder geometry detected → VIOLATED

user_message.en: This design can’t be produced — it falls into a furniture category that requires certified safety testing we don’t offer yet.

rules.test_method: product decision
rules.notes: Heuristic detection is assistive; primary control is the category system.

rules.name: MVP envelope limits
rules.description: Unit envelope limits: height ≤ 2000 mm, width ≤ 1200 mm per carcass module (wider = multiple ganged modules), depth 150–600 mm.
rules.rationale: Keeps panels within shipping limits (GLS max side 2000 mm), keeps tipping/stability risk manageable pre-testing, and stays inside one-sheet part sizes.

sources.ref: GLS CZ parcel limits (L ≤ 200 cm, girth ≤ 300 cm, ≤ 40 kg)

user_message.en: This size is outside what we can currently manufacture and deliver. Maximum height 200 cm, module width 120 cm, depth 15–60 cm.

rules.test_method: confirm with cutting partner and courier contracts

rules.name: Out-of-template designs require review
rules.description: Any design not fully expressible in the parametric template set (custom angles, curves, non-rectangular parts) is excluded or routed to manual review.
rules.rationale: MVP rule coverage and partner machining are defined only for rectangular panel geometry.

user_message.en: This design needs a human check before we can confirm it. We’ll review it and get back to you.

rules.test_method: product decision

rules.name: Supported material set
rules.description: Carcass, shelves, doors, fronts: 18 mm LTD (EN 312 P2 core). Backs: 3 mm HDF (5 mm for large backs, threshold TBD). No other materials in MVP.
rules.rationale: Single material system simplifies rules, purchasing, machining and edging. P2 is the standard furniture board for dry interiors.
rules.condition: part.material_id not allowed for part.role → VIOLATED
rules.test_method: config control

rules.name: Part must fit sheet with trim margin
rules.description: No finished part may exceed sheet format minus trim allowance: max 2740 × 2010 mm (provisional 30 mm trim per edge pair).
rules.rationale: Sheets are 2800×2070; edges must be trimmed clean before/after cutting.

user_message.en: One panel of this design is larger than the raw board we can buy. Reduce the dimension or split the part.

rules.name: Edge banding coverage
rules.description: Every exposed cut edge must be ABS-banded. Backend default: all edges of visible parts banded; hidden edges (against wall/floor, inside joints) may use 0.4 mm or remain raw only where fully concealed and moisture-safe.
rules.rationale: Raw particleboard edges are the board's weak point: they absorb moisture, chip, and release formaldehyde faster; edges must be covered (Rae p.34: 'raw edges must be covered or banded'; MDF/PB edges need filling or edgebanding).
rules.test_method: config control; edging map auto-generated

rules.name: 2 mm ABS on wear edges
rules.description: Front (user-facing) edges of doors, drawer fronts, tops and front edges of shelves get 2 mm ABS; concealed/interior edges 0.4–1 mm.
rules.rationale: Thicker banding resists impact on high-contact edges; 0.4–0.8 mm is adequate for rarely touched/hidden edges (industry guidance).

sources.ref: ABS edging thickness guidance (industry: 0.4–0.8 hidden, 1–2 mm standard/commercial, 2–3 mm heavy use)

user_message.en: Front edges get a thicker 2 mm protective edge as standard.

rules.notes: 2 mm banding may require premilling capability — confirm with edging partner (see MFG-EDGE-005).

rules.name: Décor/grain direction consistency
rules.description: For woodgrain décors, grain runs vertically on sides/doors and along the length of tops/shelves by default; all visible parts of a unit must use a consistent scheme.
rules.rationale: Visual quality; melamine board itself is direction-stable so this is aesthetic, not structural (Rae p.50: in sheet goods grain orientation doesn't matter structurally).

user_message.en: We’ve aligned the wood décor direction across the unit for a consistent look.

rules.notes: Grain direction affects nesting efficiency → price. Uni-colour décors exempt.

rules.name: Dry interior use only
rules.description: Products are for dry interior rooms. P2 board must not be sold for bathrooms/utility rooms with direct moisture exposure; care instructions must state wipe-dry cleaning.
rules.rationale: P2 is specified for furniture in dry conditions; particleboard swells irreversibly when wetted (Rae p.34).

user_message.en: This furniture is designed for dry indoor rooms. It isn’t suitable for bathrooms or damp spaces.

rules.name: Maximum unsupported shelf span (18 mm LTD)
rules.description: Hard limit: no 18 mm LTD shelf may span more than 900 mm between supports regardless of load class. Between 600 and 900 mm the deflection calculation (STRUCT-SHELF-002) governs and typically requires reduced load or a divider.
rules.rationale: Rae's span table gives 24 in (≈610 mm) as the max span for ¾-in particleboard at a moderate 20 lb/ft load on a 10-in-deep shelf — the weakest of all listed materials. 900 mm is a hard geometric cap to keep even light-load cases out of visibly sagging territory; EN 312 P2 board is bottom-of-class in stiffness (MOE 1600 N/mm²).

sources.ref: Rae p.59, 'Maximum Shelf Spans' table: particleboard ¾ in → 24 in

rules.condition: span > 900 → VIOLATED(4); span > 600 AND load_class != light → deflection calc governs

user_message.en: This shelf is too wide for 18 mm board without support. Add a vertical divider or reduce the width.

rules.suggested_fix: Insert vertical divider at midpoint (auto-proposal), or reduce width.
rules.test_method: Deflection calculation + physical load test per EN 16122 §deflection of shelves (0.65 kg/dm², 7 days) on production boards

rules.name: Shelf deflection calculation
rules.description: For every horizontal load-bearing panel compute mid-span deflection under the selected load class using simply-supported uniform-load beam theory; deflection must not exceed 1.7 mm per 300 mm of span (and never span/200).
rules.rationale: δ = 5wL⁴/(384EI) is the standard engineering model for a uniformly loaded simply supported shelf (adjustable shelves = near-simply-supported; fixed shelves are stiffer, so this is conservative). E = 1600 N/mm² (EN 312 P2 minimum). Design load default 0.65 kg/dm² (EN 16122). Sag visibility limit ~0.02 in/ft per industry practice.

sources.ref: Beam deflection formula (engineering handbooks; Woodbin Sagulator method)

rules.condition: delta_mid = 5*w*L^4/(384*E*I); I = depth*t^3/12; VIOLATED if delta_mid > min(1.7*L/300, L/200)

user_message.en: Under a full load of books this shelf would visibly sag (est. {delta} mm). Add a divider, shorten the span, or confirm you’ll load it lightly.

rules.suggested_fix: Insert divider; or reduce span; or set load class to 'light' with acknowledgement.
rules.test_method: Screening calc suitable for configurator; validate coefficients with physical EN 16122-style deflection tests incl. creep (PB creeps under sustained load — long-term factor TBD)
rules.notes: Creep factor for particleboard under sustained load is NOT included yet — a long-term multiplier (often 1.5–2× elastic deflection, tier 5) must be validated before relying on the calc near limits.

rules.name: Back panel required for racking resistance
rules.description: Every closed-carcass unit gets a full back panel fixed to sides, top and bottom. A case without a back must trigger STRUCT-BACK-004 alternative bracing or be blocked.
rules.rationale: The back closes the case and braces it against racking (Hylton p.92: 'A back closes in the case and provides bracing to keep it from racking'). Rae p.178: without a back, bottom/top droop and the case racks; the back stiffens the case and prevents sag.

user_message.en: This unit needs a back panel (or open-shelf bracing) to stay rigid and safe.

rules.test_method: doc review; racking test recommended on prototype

rules.name: Open-back units need triangulating bracing
rules.description: Deliberately open-backed shelving must include: a top rear rail/back board + a plinth/kick rail (and for tall units a second rear rail), each spanning the full width and fixed to both sides.
rules.rationale: Hylton's contemporary bookshelf 'lacks a full back, but the kickboards and back board... provide triangulation to prevent racking' (p.294).

user_message.en: Open-backed shelves need bracing rails to prevent wobble. We’ve added them to your design.

rules.test_method: Rail dimensions (width, count vs unit height) to be set by racking test/engineer — placeholder 100 mm min width, tier 6

rules.name: Vertical divider stiffens shelf and carcass
rules.description: When any shelf (incl. top/bottom panels) exceeds its allowed span, the standard fix is a full-height (or between-fixed-shelves) vertical divider connected to the panels above/below; divider positions must stack vertically so loads pass to the floor.
rules.rationale: Rae p.51: a vertical partition under a shelf/divider stiffens it and prevents sagging; joined to the case it increases overall case strength. Stacked load paths avoid loading a shelf mid-span with a divider from above.
rules.condition: divider above without support below within offset tolerance → VIOLATED(3)

user_message.en: A divider sits on an unsupported shelf. Align it with the divider below so the weight is carried to the floor.

rules.name: Minimum structural (fixed) horizontals
rules.description: Each carcass must have top and bottom structurally connected to sides with cam+dowel (or confirmat) joints, plus at least one fixed shelf or web-equivalent per 1000 mm of height (provisional). Adjustable shelves do not count as structure.
rules.rationale: Fixed shelves significantly increase carcass strength and stiffen the shelf itself (Rae p.59: fixed shelf 'much stronger than an adjustable one'); drawer dividers/fixed horizontals keep sides straight and parallel (Hylton p.89).

user_message.en: Tall units need at least one fixed shelf for rigidity. We’ve converted the middle shelf to a fixed one.

rules.test_method: Racking/side-bow test of 2 m carcass with/without mid fixed shelf

rules.name: Top/desktop overhang limit
rules.description: Applied tops may overhang the carcass ≤ 50 mm per side without extra support (provisional). Larger overhangs and all desk spans between pedestals follow the deflection calc with EN 12521-style limit (deflection ≤ span/250 for wood-based panels).
rules.rationale: Cantilevered melamine board has low bending strength; EN 12521 flags tabletop deflection > 1/250 of span for wood-based panels as requiring further testing.

sources.ref: EN 12521:2015/2023 deflection guidance (1/250 span, wood-based panels)

user_message.en: The top overhangs too far to stay flat under load. Reduce the overhang or add a support.

rules.name: Desk/table support spacing
rules.description: Desktops in 18 mm LTD must be supported (pedestal, side panel or rail) so that free span ≤ 1000 mm (provisional); spans 1000–1400 mm require a rear stiffening rail; > 1400 mm blocked pending thicker-top option (25 mm) or engineer sign-off.
rules.rationale: 18 mm PB 'bends under heavy loads' (Rae p.34). Rae p.179: cases/spans of 24 in or more supporting weight benefit from a 2-in or wider rail under the front. A desk carries point loads (monitor, leaning ~ human weight) well above shelf book loads.

sources.ref: EN 12521 strength tests exist for domestic tables (vertical static load)

user_message.en: A desk this wide needs an extra support or a rear rail so the top stays flat and solid.

rules.test_method: EN 12521 vertical static load + deflection test on prototype desk

rules.name: Geometric integrity checks
rules.description: Backend must reject: intersecting/overlapping solids; parts connected to nothing; shelves supported at one end only; doors wider than their opening; drawers colliding with shelves/dividers; back panels not reaching their fixing members.
rules.rationale: Basic physical realizability — cannot be manufactured or assembled otherwise.

user_message.en: Something in this layout physically overlaps. We’ve highlighted the conflicting parts.

rules.test_method: unit tests on geometry engine

rules.name: Stability regime trigger
rules.description: All freestanding units with height ≥ 600 mm enter the stability check pipeline (tipping calc + anchor rules), mirroring EN 14749's applicability (freestanding units ≥ 600 mm high / potential energy > 60 Nm).
rules.rationale: Aligns engine triggers with the harmonised domestic storage safety standard.

rules.name: Wall-anchor mandatory for tall/narrow units
rules.description: Units with height > 1000 mm AND height/depth > 3.0 (provisional) — and ALL units > 1500 mm high — must include a wall-attachment kit, assembly-instruction anchoring step, and a required customer acknowledgement at checkout.
rules.rationale: EN 14749: storage units must either resist overturning in defined tests (incl. doors open, loaded) or be fastened to the wall; the wall attachment and its instructions are part of compliance. Exact pass/fail can only come from testing — until then Myble anchors aggressively.

user_message.en: This unit may become unstable when loaded. Wall anchoring is required — the kit and instructions are included. Please confirm you will anchor it.

rules.test_method: EN 14749/EN 16122 stability tests (unloaded/loaded, doors open, drawers out) on representative worst-case configurations
rules.notes: Severity is 3 (acknowledged warning) for ordering, but the anchor kit itself is a non-removable backend addition (severity-4 behaviour if user tries to remove).

rules.name: Tipping-moment screening calculation
rules.description: Compute worst-case overturning: all doors open 90°, all drawers fully extended with distributed load, front toe line as pivot; compare stabilising moment (empty unit mass at COG behind pivot) vs overturning moments. Result feeds STAB-ANCHOR-002 and blocks extreme geometries (e.g. stabilising margin < 1.0 even unloaded → block).
rules.rationale: Mirrors EN 14749/EN 16122 test logic (stability with extension elements open/loaded; forces at top edge). A deterministic screening calc catches obviously dangerous geometry pre-test.

sources.ref: EN 14749 test configurations; EN 16122 stability methods; Annex D force calculation

rules.condition: margin = M_stab / M_tip; margin < 1.0 unloaded → VIOLATED(4); margin < margin_min loaded → anchor required

user_message.en: This shape would be top-heavy and unsafe even before loading. Increase the depth or reduce the height.

rules.test_method: Calibrate margin_min against physical EN-style tip tests; document load assumptions

rules.name: Multiple-drawer tall units restricted
rules.description: MVP: units taller than 800 mm may contain at most one drawer bank row unless routed to manual review; chest-of-drawers archetypes (≥3 stacked drawers, height > 800 mm) are excluded from MVP.
rules.rationale: Stacked open loaded drawers are the canonical furniture-tipover scenario targeted by storage-stability standards and recalls; Myble should not sell them before physical stability testing.

user_message.en: Designs with several stacked drawers need a manual safety review before we can accept the order.

rules.name: Shelves must not dislodge
rules.description: Adjustable shelves must sit on 4 pins with anti-slide engagement (pin with collar/locking type preferred); unloaded shelves must withstand a 100 N vertical force without falling (design provision, later verified by test).
rules.rationale: EN 14749: unloaded shelves shall not fall when tested with 100 N downward force. Pin choice determines compliance.
rules.test_method: EN 14749 shelf retention test with chosen pin SKU

rules.name: Standard MVP connection system
rules.description: Carcass corner + fixed-shelf joints: 2× cam (Minifix-15 class) + 2× dowel Ø8 per joint end (600 mm depth panels may use 3+2). Non-visible utility joints may use confirmat 7×50. Backs: screws/staples into rabbet or overlay screwed at ≤150 mm pitch (provisional). Adjustable shelves: Ø5 pins. Doors: Ø35 cup hinges. Drawers: boxed sides on 25–30 kg runners.
rules.rationale: KD (knock-down) hardware is the industry answer for furniture assembled outside the shop (Rae p.86: bolt/cam connectors 'easy to re-use'; Hylton: KD used heavily by furniture industry). One standardized system minimizes drilling patterns and errors.
rules.notes: Connector counts per joint (2/3 per end) are provisional tier-5/6 values — validate with pull/racking tests.

rules.name: Minimum hole-to-edge distances
rules.description: No connector bore may be closer than 10 mm (centre of Ø5/Ø8 bores; edge of Ø15/Ø35 bores) to any panel edge; confirmat pilots ≥ 10 mm from edge; cam housings ≥ 50 mm from panel corner (provisional); Ø35 cup edge distance per hinge spec (3–7 mm cup-to-door-edge is the spec'd exception).
rules.rationale: Particleboard blows out when fasteners are close to edges (confirmat guidance: ≥10 mm to avoid blowout). Corner distances prevent overlapping stress zones of two joints.

sources.ref: Confirmat installation guidance (≥10 mm edge distance)

user_message.en: A connector would sit too close to the panel edge here. We’ve moved it to a safe position.

rules.name: Connector spacing along joints
rules.description: Along any structural joint line, connector groups (cam+dowel) at both ends; joints longer than 450 mm (deep carcasses) get a third group mid-line (provisional). Max unfastened run 300 mm for back fixing.
rules.rationale: Prevents gap opening/racking of long joints; distributes load away from single fasteners (local stress in PB around fasteners is the failure mode).

rules.name: Hinge count and door size limits
rules.description: Door mass computed from area × board area-mass + handle allowance. ≤6 kg → 2 hinges; 6–12 kg → 3 hinges; >12 kg or width > 650 mm → blocked in MVP. Width ≤ 600 mm standard; 600–650 mm adds one hinge. Door height must exceed width (tall-narrow principle) unless horizontal flap explicitly chosen (flaps excluded MVP).
rules.rationale: Blum's published guidance: 2 hinges for 4–6 kg, 3 for 6–12 kg, valid for widths ≤600 mm; up to 650 mm add a hinge; doors should be taller than wide.

sources.ref: Blum EASY ASSEMBLY blog — Number of hinges (official Blum)
Rae p.154 (35 mm cup, styles, adjustability)

user_message.en: This door is too large for standard hinges. Split it into two doors or reduce its width.

rules.suggested_fix: Split into double doors at centre.
rules.notes: Verify against the exact hinge SKU chart in the current Blum/Hettich catalogue; opening-angle clearance vs neighbouring units still needs a geometric check (SYS32-REVEAL-006).

rules.name: Adjustable-shelf pin capacity
rules.description: Shelf design load (incl. self-weight) must not exceed 4 × rated pin load × safety factor. With Häfele K-Line 15.6 kg/pin and provisional SF 0.5: max 31 kg per shelf until validated. Load class 'heavy' on adjustable shelves > 600 mm wide → recommend fixed shelf.
rules.rationale: Pin rating is the weakest documented link after board sag; Häfele publishes 15.6 kg/item for the K-Line Ø5 support. Safety factor provisional pending pull-through tests in P2 board (pin hole bearing in PB, not pin steel, may govern).

sources.ref: Häfele K-Line shelf support datasheet (15.6 kg per item)

user_message.en: For heavy loads, a fixed shelf is sturdier than pins. Consider converting this shelf.

rules.test_method: Pin bearing test in production board per EN 16122 shelf-support strength method (0.65 kg/dm² + impact plate)

rules.name: Drawer size vs runner rating
rules.description: Drawer internal volume × density preset (utensils/clothes/paper) + drawer self-weight must stay under runner dynamic rating (25–30 kg class). Drawer width max 900 mm; nominal runner length ≤ cabinet depth − 10 mm (provisional clearance).
rules.rationale: Runner families publish dynamic load classes (Blum TANDEM 30/50 kg). Width and depth constraints come from the runner's published application limits.

user_message.en: This drawer exceeds the load rating of our runners. Make it smaller or split it into two.

rules.name: Re-assembly durability policy
rules.description: Joints intended for possible customer re-assembly (moving flats) use cam+dowel. Confirmats are single-assembly: instructions must warn against repeated full unscrew/re-drive cycles in the same hole (max 2–3 cycles, provisional).
rules.rationale: Cam connectors are 'very easy to re-use... through many cycles' (Rae p.86); screws driven directly into particleboard degrade the hole (PB screw-holding rated Poor, Rae p.33).

user_message.en: Planning to move often? This unit’s main joints can be taken apart and rebuilt repeatedly.

rules.name: 32 mm system holes
rules.description: All adjustable-shelf pin holes and hinge-plate/runner fixing positions derive from vertical rows of Ø5 mm holes at 32 mm pitch; front row axis 37 mm from the front edge, back row 37 mm from the back edge (or fixed offset for shallow carcasses).
rules.rationale: The European 32 mm system standardizes drilling so hinges, runners and pins all land on the same grid (Rae p.154: cup hinges 'part of the gear used in the 32mm cabinetry system in Europe'); 37 mm front setback and 32 mm pitch are the system convention.

sources.ref: 32 mm system references (True32/Festool guide, Wikipedia system description)

rules.notes: Exact setback may follow partner's boring machine template (35/37 mm variants exist) — freeze with partner.

rules.name: Shelf positions snap to grid
rules.description: User-dragged shelf/divider positions snap to the nearest 32 mm hole position; free positioning is not offered for adjustable shelves.
rules.rationale: Adjustable shelves physically exist only at hole positions; snapping prevents impossible states instead of erroring afterwards.

user_message.en: Shelf positions follow the 32 mm hole grid — we’ve snapped it to the nearest position.

rules.name: Door/front gaps and reveals
rules.description: Frameless overlay fronts: 2 mm gap between neighbouring fronts and at unit perimeter (provisional 2–3 mm); door must clear adjacent walls/units when opening (hinge crank geometry check); inset fronts excluded from MVP.
rules.rationale: Frameless (Euro) cabinets rely on consistent reveals; insufficient gaps cause binding given board tolerance + hinge adjustment range (cup hinges adjust in 3 axes — Rae p.154).

rules.name: Back panel integration method
rules.description: MVP default: 3 mm HDF back overlaid into a rebate OR surface-screwed to carcass rear edges (partner capability decides; one method frozen per partner profile). Grooved-in backs only if partner mills grooves.
rules.rationale: Backs set into rabbets are traditional (Hylton p.333: '1/4-in plywood back' set into rabbets; Rae p.50 'rabbet side for back'); surface-screwed overlay back is the simplest RTA method and adds the same racking function if screwed at close pitch.

rules.name: Plinth/toe-kick geometry
rules.description: Optional toe-kick: depth 64 mm, height 114 mm, each adjustable ±25 mm (converted from Rae's comfortable kick space 2½ in × 4½ in ± 1 in). Alternatively adjustable feet + clip-on plinth.
rules.rationale: Rae p.184: comfortable kick space x=2½ in, y=4½ in, adjustable ±1 in.

user_message.en: The recessed base (toe-kick) uses ergonomic standard dimensions.

rules.name: Minimum machinable part size
rules.description: No edgebanded part smaller than 160 × 85 mm (conservative union of common edgebander minima); absolute minimum any part 100 × 50 mm pending partner confirmation.
rules.rationale: Industrial edgebanders list minimum workpiece ~140–160 mm length and 70–85 mm width (Biesse Akron 440: 140×85; Brandt Ambition 1440: 160×70).

user_message.en: A part of this design is too small to manufacture safely by machine. Increase its size.

rules.name: Cutting & drilling tolerances
rules.description: Engine assumes: cut length/width ±0.5 mm (target ±0.3), drilling position ±0.3 mm, squareness ≤ 0.5 mm/m (all provisional until partner data). Design clearances must absorb worst-case stack-up: e.g. drawer box side clearance ≥ 2 × cut tolerance + runner spec clearance.
rules.rationale: Every fit rule (drawer clearances, reveals, back rebates) must reference a single tolerance table; values are typical industry but partner-specific.

rules.name: Hole pattern feasibility
rules.description: No overlapping bores; min web 8 mm between adjacent hole walls (provisional); Ø35 cup bores only in ≥16 mm panels; no through-bores where a visible face must stay clean; all drilling from at most 2 setups per part (cost cap, provisional).
rules.rationale: Preserves board integrity around bores (local stress, PB crumbles between close holes) and machine efficiency.

rules.name: Edging process constraints
rules.description: Edging sequence auto-generated (band before drilling reference edges per partner flow); 2 mm ABS allowed only if partner supports it (premill recommended); banding overhang trimmed flush; banded dimension = cut dimension + 2×band thickness accounted in cutting list.
rules.rationale: Edge-band thickness changes finished part dimensions — cutting lists must compensate or reveals/fits will be off by up to 4 mm on double-banded parts.

sources.ref: practice; Rae p.79 (banding sized wider than panel, trimmed flush)

rules.name: Part labelling & orientation marks
rules.description: Every part gets a printed label: order ID, part ID, orientation arrow ('top/front'), and step reference matching the instructions. Symmetric-looking parts with asymmetric drilling must carry an explicit 'THIS SIDE UP/FRONT' mark.
rules.rationale: Error-proofing for non-professional assemblers; hole patterns on near-symmetric parts are the top RTA assembly failure.

rules.name: Complexity cap per order
rules.description: Caps (provisional): ≤ 60 parts per unit, ≤ 25 unique part geometries, ≤ 12 drilling patterns; beyond caps → manual review for quotability.
rules.rationale: Protects partners and margins from pathological configurator output.

user_message.en: This design is unusually complex — we’ll review it and confirm the price and lead time.

rules.name: Feasible assembly sequence must exist
rules.description: Engine must derive a valid ordered sequence (carcass → fixed shelves/dividers → back → feet → doors/drawers → shelves) with no trapped parts: a part whose connectors cannot be reached/engaged after prior steps invalidates the design.
rules.rationale: Classic trapped-assembly errors (e.g. fixed shelf between two already-cammed panels with no insertion path) make kits unbuildable at home.

user_message.en: This combination of fixed parts couldn’t be assembled in any order. We’ve highlighted the conflict.

rules.test_method: unit tests + prototype builds

rules.name: Tool access clearance
rules.description: Every cam must be rotatable (screwdriver axis clearance ≥ 120 mm above the cam face, provisional); every confirmat drivable (straight-line access); compartments smaller than 120×120 mm may not contain in-compartment fasteners.
rules.rationale: No-tool-access is a common CAD-to-reality failure; cams face inside the carcass.
rules.test_method: Prototype assembly trials

rules.name: Customer toolkit is fixed
rules.description: Designs may only require: PZ2 screwdriver, supplied hex key, hammer (soft tap for dowels/HDF nails), spirit level (recommended). No glue, no drill for furniture assembly. Wall anchoring is the single exception (drill required; communicated separately).
rules.rationale: Home-assembly promise; KD hardware exists precisely to avoid glue-ups outside the shop (Rae p.86; Hylton KD discussion).

user_message.en: Everything assembles with the included key and a screwdriver. Wall anchoring needs a drill.

rules.name: Two-person flag
rules.description: Flag '2 people recommended' when: any single panel > 15 kg or > 1800 mm, or assembled unit > 35 kg, or unit must be tilted upright from horizontal (see ASM-TILT-005). (All provisional.)
rules.rationale: Manual handling ergonomics; melamine panels are dense (~11–12 kg/m² at 18 mm).

user_message.en: This product is easier and safer to assemble with two people.

rules.name: Tilt-up ceiling clearance
rules.description: Tall carcasses are assembled lying down and tilted upright. Tip diagonal = √(height² + depth²). If customer provides room height and diagonal exceeds it minus 20 mm, warn and offer reduced height or upright-assembly instructions.
rules.rationale: Same clearance logic cabinetmakers use for built-ins (Hylton p.343: sides made 2–3 in shorter than ceiling height so cases can be set up easily).

user_message.en: Heads up: at {h} cm tall and {d} cm deep, this unit needs {diag} cm of ceiling height to tilt upright after assembly.

rules.name: Per-order generated instructions
rules.description: Every order ships with instructions generated from the exact design: exploded views per step, part labels matching physical labels, fastener counts, anchor step for STAB-ANCHOR designs, and a spare-parts QR (part IDs orderable individually).
rules.rationale: Custom furniture cannot use generic manuals; replacement-part logic requires stable part IDs.

rules.name: Panel length vs carrier limits
rules.description: Carrier profiles (validate before launch): GLS CZ ≤ 2000 mm longest side, girth (2H+2W+L) ≤ 3000 mm, ≤ 40 kg; PPL private ≤ 1000×500×500; DPD ≤ 31.5 kg, pickup ≤ 1000 mm; Packeta ≤ 120/150 cm dim-sum, ≤ 10 kg. Engine selects cheapest feasible carrier per package; if no parcel carrier fits → pallet freight path (MVP: manual review).
rules.rationale: Panel length is the binding constraint for flat-pack; GLS's 2 m limit is what allows wardrobe-height sides (1950 mm max practical).

user_message.en: Reducing the height by {x} cm would let this ship as a standard parcel and save on delivery.

rules.notes: Carrier terms change; limits must live in a dated carrier profile, re-verified quarterly.

rules.name: Package mass cap & split logic
rules.description: Target ≤ 25 kg per package (hard cap 30 kg, provisional under carrier 31.5/40 limits for handling safety); orders auto-split into panel packs + hardware kit; each pack's contents recorded; kit-to-pack compatibility check ensures no pack depends on a part in a missing pack.
rules.rationale: 31.5 kg is a common carrier cap (PPL/DPD) but two-person lifting guidance argues for ~25 kg packs; splitting logic prevents partial-delivery deadlock.

rules.name: Edge & surface protection
rules.description: Melamine faces packed face-to-face with interleaf; all four corners of each pack get corner protectors; banded front edges padded; 3 mm HDF backs packed inside stiff panel sandwich; packaging allowance per side (provisional 20 mm) added to package dims.
rules.rationale: Laminated PB edges/corners chip on impact and are unrepairable; thin HDF bends (Rae p.34 fragility of faced panels; general packaging practice).
rules.test_method: ISTA-style drop/transport test on representative pack

rules.name: Shippability economics surfaced
rules.description: If a small dimension change (≤ 30 mm) would move the order into a cheaper shipping class, surface the saving as a tip; if shipping cost > X% of product price (provisional 25%), show notice.
rules.rationale: Converts logistics constraints into design guidance instead of checkout surprise.

user_message.en: Reducing the width by {x} mm would make this design suitable for standard parcel delivery.

rules.name: Severity → UI behaviour mapping
rules.description: 0: passive info; 1: dismissible tip; 2: highlighted recommendation with one-click fix; 3: modal acknowledgement stored with order; 4: red state, cart blocked, fix path shown; 5: review request flow with SLA message. Silent prevention (snapping, min limits in sliders) is preferred over post-hoc errors wherever the constraint is continuous.
rules.rationale: Users should mostly never see raw rule violations — sliders and snapping keep them in valid space; messages reserve attention for real decisions.

rules.name: Acknowledgements are recorded
rules.description: Every severity-3 acknowledgement stores: rule_id, rules version, message text shown, timestamp, user/session; re-triggered if design changes invalidate a prior acknowledgement.
rules.rationale: Traceability for safety communications (wall anchoring, load limits).

rules.name: AI may explain, never decide
rules.description: LLM features may rephrase findings, answer questions and propose design ideas, but every AI proposal is re-validated by the deterministic engine before it can be applied; AI output can never mark a design safe, override severity, or edit thresholds.
rules.rationale: Safety/manufacturability must be auditable and reproducible; LLMs are not.
